rounds.proof_sketch: For input shape [128, 4000] with dim=1: outer_size=128, dim_size=4000, inner_size=1. Block configuration: dim3 block_size_dim(min(256, 1)) = dim3(1), so blockDim.x=1, blockDim.y=1. With single-threaded blocks: threadIdx.x=0 and threadIdx.y=0 for ALL threads. Original loop: for(inner_idx=0; inner_idx<1; inner_idx+=1). Mutant loop: for(inner_idx=0; inner_idx<1; inner_idx+=1). Both are identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes threadIdx.x to threadIdx.y in the loop initialization, but the kernel launch configuration forces equivalence. With input shape [128, 4000] and dim=1, inner_size=1 is computed. The block size is set to min(256, inner_size)=min(256,1)=1, creating effectively single-threaded blocks where blockDim.x=1 and blockDim.y=1. In CUDA, both threadIdx.x and threadIdx.y are 0 when there's only one thread per block. Since both indices start at 0, increment by the same blockDim.x=1, and check against the same inner_size=1, the loop behavior is identical. Every inner position (just position 0) is processed exactly once by both versions.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed configuration. The only way to expose the difference would be to use dim=0 (making inner_size=4000, which would give blockDim.x=256 and cause threadIdx.y to always be 0 while threadIdx.x varies), but this requires changing the model configuration, which is not allowed under the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing CUDA thread index mutations, ensure the test configuration exercises multi-threaded block scenarios. For this kernel, testing with dim=0 on the [128, 4000] tensor would create inner_size=4000 and blockDim.x=256, which would expose the threadIdx.x vs threadIdx.y difference. Mutation testing frameworks should consider varying operation dimensions (like cumsum dim) as part of the configuration space, not just input values.
